metadata.title: OneXp Mobile Devs Command Toolkit — Complete Termux Operations Reference
metadata.description: Every Termux command you need for web and app development on Android.
metadata.author: Amos Isaiah Tizhe — OneXportal

categories.title: Setup & First Steps
categories.description: The very first commands you run after installing Termux. Get your environment ready for development.

commands.title: Update & upgrade all packages
commands.description: Updates the package list and upgrades everything to the latest version. Run this first on any fresh Termux install.
commands.howToUse: Run immediately after installing Termux. Press Enter to keep defaults when prompted.
commands.whenToUse: Very first command on a new install, and periodically to keep tools updated and secure.
commands.tip: 💡 If asked about config file changes during upgrade, press Enter to keep the installed version.

commands.title: Grant storage permission
commands.description: Requests access to Android's internal storage. Creates ~/storage/ with shortcuts to Downloads, DCIM, Music, etc.
commands.howToUse: Run once → tap "Allow" in the popup. Access files at ~/storage/shared/ or ~/storage/downloads/
commands.whenToUse: Once after fresh install. Required to share files between Termux, Acode, and your file manager.

commands.title: Install the full dev toolkit
commands.code: pkg install git nodejs python openssh curl wget nano zip unzip -y
commands.description: Installs Git, Node.js/npm, Python, SSH, curl, wget, nano, zip, and unzip in one shot. Your complete baseline stack.
commands.whenToUse: One-time setup on a fresh Termux. After this you can do web dev, scripting, and version control immediately.

commands.title: Create your dev workspace
commands.description: Creates an organized workspace and navigates into it. All your projects should live here for consistency.
commands.whenToUse: After initial Termux setup. Every new project and git clone should land under ~/dev/projects/

commands.title: Show Termux environment info
commands.description: Displays Termux version, Android version, CPU architecture, and installed package count.
commands.whenToUse: Troubleshooting, reporting bugs, or verifying your environment before starting a project.

commands.title: List all installed packages
commands.description: Lists every package currently installed in your Termux environment with its installed version.
commands.whenToUse: Auditing your environment or checking if a specific tool is already installed before reinstalling.

categories.title: Package Manager (pkg)
categories.description: Install, remove, search, and manage all software in Termux using the pkg command — a friendly wrapper around apt.

commands.title: Install a package
commands.description: Installs any available package. -y auto-confirms all prompts without interaction.
commands.howToUse: Replace package-name: git, nodejs, python, vim, ffmpeg, mariadb, php, etc.
commands.whenToUse: Every time you need a new tool, language runtime, or CLI in Termux.

commands.title: Remove a package
commands.description: Removes an installed package from Termux, freeing storage space on your device.
commands.whenToUse: When you no longer need a tool — especially useful on phones with limited storage.

commands.title: Search for a package
commands.description: Searches the available package repo for matching names or keywords. Partial names work fine.
commands.howToUse: Try: pkg search java  |  pkg search http  |  pkg search image
commands.whenToUse: When you don't know the exact package name or want to discover available tools.

categories.title: Navigation & Folders
categories.description: Move around the filesystem and manage directories with professional efficiency.

commands.title: Go to home directory
commands.description: Returns to Termux home (/data/data/com.termux/files/home). The ~ always refers to home.
commands.whenToUse: When lost deep in directories and need to return to your base. Plain "cd" works too.

commands.title: List files with full details
commands.description: Lists all files including hidden ones, with permissions, human-readable sizes, and timestamps. The most informative listing format.
commands.howToUse: ls = simple. ls -la = detailed + hidden. ls -lah = detailed + human sizes. ls -lt = sorted by time.
commands.whenToUse: Before any operation on a folder — always check what's actually there first.

commands.title: Print current directory path
commands.description: Prints the full absolute path of your current location. Removes all ambiguity about where you are.
commands.whenToUse: Before running any destructive command. Also useful for copying the current path.

commands.title: Create nested project structure
commands.description: Creates a project folder with multiple subdirectories using brace expansion. One command, full structure.
commands.whenToUse: Scaffolding a new project without a framework CLI — create the entire directory tree instantly.

commands.title: Remove a folder and all contents
commands.description: Permanently deletes a folder and everything inside it. Irreversible — no recycle bin in Termux.
commands.howToUse: Always confirm with pwd and ls first. Never run rm -rf ~ or rm -rf /
commands.whenToUse: Deleting node_modules, old build dirs, or entire project folders you no longer need.
commands.tip: ⚠️ Double-check the name before pressing Enter. This permanently deletes everything inside.

categories.title: File Operations
categories.description: Create, copy, move, rename, and delete files. The everyday operations you'll run on every project.

commands.title: Create empty files
commands.description: Creates one or more empty files at once. If a file already exists, updates its timestamp without changing content.
commands.whenToUse: Starting any new component, config file, or script you'll edit in Acode right after.

commands.title: Create a file with content
commands.description: Creates a file and writes text into it. > overwrites. >> appends to an existing file without overwriting.
commands.howToUse:
echo "text" > file — create/overwrite.
echo "text" >> file — append a line.
commands.whenToUse: Seeding config files, adding lines to .env, or writing a quick script stub from the terminal.

commands.title: Copy a file or directory
commands.code:
cp source.js destination.js
cp -r src/ src-backup/
commands.description: Copies files or entire directories. -r is required for directories.
commands.howToUse: cp .env.example .env — copy a template to create your local config file.
commands.whenToUse: Creating backups, duplicating files, or copying templates before editing.

commands.title: Move or rename a file
commands.code:
mv old-name.js new-name.js
mv component.jsx src/components/
commands.description: Moves a file to a new path or renames it. Works for both files and directories.
commands.whenToUse: Refactoring project structure, renaming components, or reorganizing files during development.

commands.title: Delete a file
commands.code:
rm filename.js
rm -i filename.js   # with confirmation prompt
commands.description: Permanently deletes a file. Cannot be undone — Termux has no recycle bin. Use -i for a confirmation prompt.
commands.whenToUse: Removing old files, generated artifacts, or temporary files no longer needed in your project.

categories.title: View & Read Files
categories.description: Read file contents, inspect logs, count lines, search text, and check disk usage from the terminal.

commands.title: Print full file contents
commands.description: Outputs a file's entire contents to the terminal. Best for short files — configs, .env, package.json, .gitignore.
commands.whenToUse: Quick checks on small files. For large files use head, tail, or less instead to avoid flooding the terminal.

commands.title: View first N lines
commands.description: Shows only the first N lines. Default is 10. Ideal for previewing large files or log headers without loading everything.
commands.whenToUse: Checking file structure, import headers, or the first entries of a large log file.

commands.title: View last N lines + follow mode
commands.code:
tail -50 app.log
# Live follow — shows new lines as written:
tail -f app.log
commands.description: Shows the last N lines. -f follows the file in real-time — essential for monitoring live server logs. Press Ctrl+C to stop.
commands.whenToUse: Monitoring a running server, reading error logs, or watching a build process output live.

commands.title: Search text inside files (grep)
commands.code:
grep -rn "TODO" ./src
grep -ri "console.log" .          # case-insensitive
grep -rl "import React" .         # filenames only
commands.description: Recursively searches all files for a string. -r = recursive, -n = line numbers, -i = case-insensitive, -l = filenames only.
commands.whenToUse: Finding all TODOs, tracking function usage, auditing console.logs before a production push.

commands.title: Count lines / words / bytes
commands.code:
wc -l filename.js
wc -l src/*.js   # multiple files with total
commands.description: -l counts lines, -w counts words, -c counts bytes. Works on multiple files and shows a grand total.
commands.whenToUse: Checking file sizes, counting rows in a dataset, or seeing how large your codebase has grown.
